title: The Share a Travel Protection Plans Certificate Takes Back
content:
These questions are answered for the share which a Travel Protection Plans certificate takes back of what a supplier has paid the traveller. Two figures from the certificate's own claim record decide it: the largest payment the certificate has settled, and the largest deductible withheld from its settled payments.

**Where a deductible was withheld from the payment the certificate settled and the supplier has paid the traveller more than that payment, what is the share which the certificate takes back?**

It is 85 per cent, because the traveller bore the deductible themselves and keeps that share of what the supplier paid.

**Where a deductible was withheld from the payment the certificate settled and the supplier has paid the traveller that payment or less, what is the share which the certificate takes back?**

It is 70 per cent.

**Where neither of those holds, what is the share which the certificate takes back?**

It is the whole of it, 100 per cent.

## The three cases

| Deductible withheld from the payment the certificate settled | What the supplier has paid, set against that payment | Share the certificate takes back |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Above nothing | More than that payment | 85 per cent |
| Above nothing | That payment or less | 70 per cent |
| Nothing withheld | Either way | 100 per cent |

**Which payment is meant by the payment the certificate settled?**

The largest payment the certificate has settled, and the deductible set against it is the largest deductible withheld from its settled payments.

**Where does the boundary between the first two cases fall?**

At equality. Where the supplier has paid exactly the amount of that payment, the second case applies and the share is 70 per cent; the first case, at 85 per cent, requires the supplier to have paid strictly more.

**Where no deductible was withheld at all, do the amounts matter?**

No. Both of the first two cases require a deductible above nothing to have been withheld. Where none was, the third case is reached whatever the supplier paid, and the certificate takes back the whole of it at 100 per cent.
